intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-11-01). Dancing is a fun and exciting way to express yourself, stay active, and connect with others. Every style of dance, from hip hop and ballet to cultural and partner dances, has its own rhythm, history, and story to tell. In the Dance Test Lab Badge, you’ll learn how to move safely, warm up properly, and understand what makes every dance unique. You’ll explore different styles of dance, learn about famous dancers, and even perform your own routine. Whether you’re new to dancing or already love it, this badge will help you build confidence, creativity, and coordination while having a great time moving to the beat.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

requirements.req_text: Preventing Injury. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor how you can prevent injuries while participating in dancing activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. Explain what you need to take into consideration before trying potentially dangerous moves including but not limited to jumps, flips, and lifts. (b) Explain to your counselor how to appropriately warm-up prior to dancing activities to protect joints and prevent injury. Demonstrate three dance warm-ups. (c) Show that you know first aid for injuries that could occur while dancing, including cuts, scratches, abrasions, concussions, blisters, sprains, stress fractures, tendonitis, and back injuries. (d) Explain the importance of wearing the right clothing and gear for dance, including appropriate footwear.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
quiz_item.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

requirements.req_text: Research. Research TWO of the types of dance you learned about in requirement 3 by doing the following for EACH type of dance you chose: (a) Give a brief history, including its origin, how it came to be in the United States if it originated elsewhere, and where in the world/country it is most often performed. (b) Name/describe different variations of this style of dancing, if any. (c) Name some specific types of dance steps/moves particular to this type of dance. Does this dance tell a story through movement? If so, please describe. (d) Include information on at least one person who became well-known performing, teaching, or choreographing this type of dance. (e) Note if anyone with a physical disability (such a person with hearing or sight impairment or a person who uses a wheelchair) could participate in this type of dancing. What accommodations would that person need to participate? (f) Locate and share a place near you/in your state where you could watch or participate in this type of dance as a part of a performance, competition, or class. Find out when and where this is offered and what the cost would be to watch or participate. (g) Watch a performance of this type of dance and discuss with your counselor. (While viewing an in-person performance is preferable, a recorded performance may also be permitted.)

requirements.req_text: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following: (a) Learn a dance. Use at least THREE types of warm-ups prior to your routine to prepare different muscle groups for the exercise. The dance may be solo, group, or partner dance and can use a memorized choreographed routine or an improvised dance. It should be a minimum of 2 minutes long or several shorter dances that add up to at least 2 minutes. The dance should demonstrate at least three different dance moves/steps and should contain music with Scout-appropriate lyrics, if applicable. (b) Perform the dance for your counselor or submit a video of your performance to your counselor. Describe to your counselor what precautions you took to avoid injury before and during your performance. Name or describe the 3 different dance moves that you learned, the 3 different warm-ups you chose, and the 5 Elements of Dance in your routine.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When a choreographer contrasts a sharp, sudden punch with a slow, floating arm sweep, which element of dance is primarily being varied?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When a choreographer contrasts a sharp, sudden punch with a slow, floating arm sweep, which element of dance is primarily being varied?
options: A. Floor pathway
B. Energy
C. Group formation
D. Stage lighting
choices: A. Floor pathway
B. Energy
C. Group formation
D. Stage lighting
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Energy governs how movement happens, distinguishing between percussive, sustained, swinging, suspended, or collapsing movement qualities (p. 10).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which dance style relies on a caller prompting four couples arranged in a quadrangle through specific movement figures?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which dance style relies on a caller prompting four couples arranged in a quadrangle through specific movement figures?
options: A. Aerial silks
B. Breakdancing
C. Square dancing
D. Classical ballet
choices: A. Aerial silks
B. Breakdancing
C. Square dancing
D. Classical ballet
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Square dancing is a group social dance for four couples arranged in a square who execute steps announced live by a caller (p. 18).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do dancers with hearing impairments often stay synchronized with musical timing during a performance?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do dancers with hearing impairments often stay synchronized with musical timing during a performance?
options: A. By performing only in total silence without any rhythmic structure
B. By avoiding group choreography and dancing exclusively alone
C. By keeping their eyes closed throughout the entire routine
D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts
choices: A. By performing only in total silence without any rhythmic structure
B. By avoiding group choreography and dancing exclusively alone
C. By keeping their eyes closed throughout the entire routine
D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Dancers with hearing impairments commonly sense low-frequency sound vibrations through sprung wooden floors and coordinate with ensemble visual cues and internal counts (p. 24).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before performing your learned dance for Requirement 5, what preparation must you complete to protect your body?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before performing your learned dance for Requirement 5, what preparation must you complete to protect your body?
options: A. Drink an energy beverage five minutes before stepping onto the floor
B. Practice the routine once at double speed without stopping
C. Complete at least three types of warmups targeting different muscle groups
D. Tape both ankles tightly so the joints cannot bend
choices: A. Drink an energy beverage five minutes before stepping onto the floor
B. Practice the routine once at double speed without stopping
C. Complete at least three types of warmups targeting different muscle groups
D. Tape both ankles tightly so the joints cannot bend
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Complete at least three types of warmups targeting different muscle groups
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Preparing different muscle groups with at least three distinct warmup exercises increases elasticity and coordination prior to executing your routine (p. 28).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which dance-related professional specializes in rehabilitating injured performers and designing conditioning programs to prevent future injuries?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which dance-related professional specializes in rehabilitating injured performers and designing conditioning programs to prevent future injuries?
options: A. Dance notation archivist
B. Performing arts physical therapist
C. Theatrical lighting designer
D. Music copyright attorney
choices: A. Dance notation archivist
B. Performing arts physical therapist
C. Theatrical lighting designer
D. Music copyright attorney
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Performing arts physical therapists combine clinical medical training with biomechanics knowledge to treat and prevent injuries in dancers (p. 35).
